summary: The package-backed Scene.SvgBrowser browser runner extends the existing hosted public-circle document constructor with a test-only affine zoom wrapper. Its bounded shared-symbol and expanded-geometry witness alternates two/six units through six deterministic spawn/despawn and pan/zoom cycles, requiring retained unaffected unit/glyph/definition identity, native viewport picking, complete off-viewport export, bounded owned DOM and synchronous listener/frame requests, definition removal across representations, and disposal. Real-browser DOM controls inject stale nodes and definitions, reconstruct retained owners and hide geometry; each must be rejected by the same witness. Document-host source has no simulation revision or listener/frame ownership API. Its synchronous ownership instrumentation is bounded to calls into that host and uses known listener/frame positive controls; it does not measure heap/GPU memory. The existing retained-host cameraRevisionControl supplies the separate actual simulation revision correspondence assertion. This record captures source boundaries, not browser execution or performance acceptance. Original local launch failures (missing browser installation, then missing libnspr4 on the Arch host) remain environmental failures; the existing hosted Ubuntu browser workflow is the software qualification route. Parent programme acceptance, native/GPU, accessibility, licensed fixtures, publication and installed/product adoption remain separate.
title: Public-circle viewport and churn witness uses document-host ownership, not simulation revisions
